body_html:
A couple of years ago I created a small e-commerce solution, with a data-model based on Schema.org’s “Product”-schema.
A lot has happened since then.

So, what is Schema.org?

Schema.org was created in 2011 by Google, Microsoft and Yahoo, in order to create a standard for all the various microdata-formats that existed at the time: Microformats, FOAF, OpenSyc, hCard etc.

Search engines including Bing, Google, Yahoo! and Yandex rely on this markup to improve the display of search results, making it easier for people to find the right Web pages

Schema-based markup basically enriches the html, providing search-engines with more detailed information about for instance a person, a product, a recipe or an event.

When a search-engine displays this enriched markup,  it’s called rich snippets.

Schemas

Visit schema.org/docs/schemas.html for a complete list of schemas. New schemas are added often, and the existing schemas extended, so re-visit the site from time to time.

As an example, I’m going to markup a commercial product (e-commerce) using the following schemas:

Product
ImageObject
AggregateRating
Offer
itemCondition
Rating
Review

The Product-schema alone is rather big, so I’m going to use only subsets of the various schema’s features.

Model
name Product name (should also be the title of the page as well as og:title*)
description Product description
productID A unique product-identifier
itemCondition Possible values:
DamagedCondition
NewCondition
RefurbishedCondition
UsedCondition
other color, depth, height, width, weight
image ImageObject (should also be og:image*):
contentUrl
name
copyrightHolder
copyrightYear
representativeOfPage
aggregateRating Review/rating overview:
ratingValue
reviewCount
offer price
availability
review name
author
description
datePublished
reviewRating (Rating schema)
ratingValue

*) Open Graph meta properties: More on ogp.me.

There are many more itemprops in the schemas, go and have a look at the documentation. For instance, in order to limit your product to a specific gender or age-group, use the PeopleAudience-schema.

Example Markup

The tags can be whatever you want, as long as they are semantically correct!
The important thing here are the itemtype, itemscope and itemprop-attributes.

<article itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Product">
  <h1 itemprop="name">Captain America #425</h1>
  
  <figure itemprop="image" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject">
    <img src="425.jpg" itemprop="contentUrl" alt="Captain America #425" />
    <meta itemprop="thumbnail" content="425.jpg" />
    <figcaption>
      <span itemprop="name">Captain America #425</span>
      <span itemprop="copyrightHolder">Marvel Comics</span>
      <span itemprop="copyrightYear">1994</span>
      <meta itemprop="representativeOfPage" content="true">
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  
  <div itemprop="aggregateRating" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/AggregateRating">
   Rated <span itemprop="ratingValue">3</span>/5
   based on <span itemprop="reviewCount">11</span> customer reviews
  </div>

  <div itemprop="offers" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Offer">
    <span itemprop="price">$1.99</span>
    <link itemprop="availability" href="http://schema.org/InStock" />In stock
  </div>
  
  <span itemprop="itemCondition" content="NewCondition">New</span>
    
  <strong>Product description:</strong>
  <span itemprop="description">
    ...
  </span>

  <h2>Customer reviews:</h2>
  <div itemprop="review" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Review">
    <span itemprop="name">It all starts here!</span> -
    by <span itemprop="author">Avid reader</span>,
    <meta itemprop="datePublished" content="2011-04-01">April 1, 2011
    <div itemprop="reviewRating" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Rating">
      <span itemprop="ratingValue">5</span>
    </div>
    <span itemprop="description">
      ...
    </span>
  </div>
</article>

Google search-result output


Pretty nifty, huh? Google might even display a thumbnail-image next to the result.

Tools & Testing

To verify the markup for your rich snippets, both Google and Microsoft provide online tools:

Google Rich Snippets Tool
Bing Validator

Bing’s Validator is in beta and rather limited compared to Googles.

The above example is available here: stoumann.dk/examples/schema/

Click here to view all the data, Googles Rich Snippets Tool can extract from the example markup.

Styling the output

Bonus-info. You can use the itemprop-attributes directly for styling — no need to add additional classes:

[itemprop="availability"] { 
  color: green; 
}

/* Insert a copyright symbol */
[itemprop="copyrightHolder"]:before { 
  content: "\00a9\0020"; 
}

[itemprop="price"] { 
  color: maroon; 
}
etc.

Happy coding!
